 JUDGMENT

The petitioners have filed this claim petition against respondents seeking compensation on account of death of the deceased Sri.R.Karthik @ Rajendra Karthik S/o late K.Rajendran, who died in Motor Vehicle Accident.
The brief facts of the case of the petitioners is as under:

On 09.12.2020 the deceased R.Karthik and his wife and son were going towards Tirupathi from Rly Kodur Town, in a Car bearing No.AP39BU0203 driven by deceased R.Karthik and said car belongs to family friends of deceased.
On the way at about 11.00 p.m at Ghatt Road, near Kukkaladoddi Village, Rly Kodur Mandal, YSR Kadapa District, Andra Pradesh, due to mechanical defect, the car dashed road divider.

Due to impact the car was capsized and all the occupants of the car caught inside and sustained grievous injuries and J.Uma Maheswari and R.Karthik i.e.,
parents of petitioner No.1 succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
The accident was occurred due to carelessness, rash and negligent driving of the Car by its driver.
The petitioner No.2 has spent Rs.50,000/ towards transportation of deadbody and funeral obsequies.
Prior to accident the deceased was hale and healthy and was aged 38 years and was businessman and earning Rs.50,000/ p.m and the petitioners are entirely depending upon the earnings of the deceased.
Due to death of the deceased.
The petitioner No.1 who is the minor son of the deceased put to lot of mental agony and untold misery and lost the love and (SCCH3) 4 M.V.C.No.702/2021 affection and he became orphan.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the Car is liable to pay compensation of Rs.15,00,000/ towards personal accident coverage towards the owner of the vehicle.

Hence, pray to allow the petition.
03.
On service of notice, the respondent No.2 has appeared before the tribunal through its counsel and filed written statement.
Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 did not appeared and hence, was placed exparte.

04. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has contended that the claim petition is not maintainable as the deceased himself was the tortfeasor and as per Charge sheet, Police investigating authorities have filed Charge sheet against deceased R.Karthik, the petitioners have filed claim petition U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, the alleged accident said to have occurred due to rash and negligent driving of deceased R.Karthik and petitioners claims to be legal representative of the deceased Karthik, hence, claim petition U/Sec 166 is not maintainable as the deceased himself was Kirthikeswar U vs T.V.Srinivasulu on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113504340/
2 the tortfeasor and as such petition is liable to be dismissed.
The petitioners need to prove no negligence on the part of the deceased.

Hence, claim petition is liable to be dismissed and (SCCH3)
5 M.V.C.No.702/2021 same is devoid of merits and admits the issuance of the policy in favour of respondent No.1 for the vehicle Car bearing No.AP39BU0203, but the same is subject to terms and conditions of the policy and as on the face of the prosecution papers reveals it is a self accident by the driver of the insured car and as such the question of coverage of liability to the petitioners by indemnifying the respondent No.1 does not arise at all under the personal accident coverage of Rs.15,00,000/ as claimed and also this is not a proper forum and hence, the liability is not admitted and claim against this respondent be dismissed as not maintainable and denied the entire case of the petitioners and denied alleged accident, age, occupation, income of deceased and expenses incurred by the petitioners and and also denied that deceased sustained fatal injuries in the alleged accident by driving insured car and the driver did not possess valid driving licence as on the date of accident and it is further contended that the place of accident is in the State of Andhra Pradesh, the Policy issuing office is at Delhi and owner is from Karnoon District of Andhra Pradesh State.

Hence, this Court has no jurisdiction to entertain the petition and the petition U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act is not maintainable, since Charge sheet is (SCCH3) 6 M.V.C.No.702/2021 against the deceased Karthik himself and due to his own negligence the alleged accident said to have occurred.
Hence, claim petition be dismissed as the tortfeasor is not entitle for compensation and the compensation claimed is exorbitant.
Hence, pray for dismiss the petition against this respondent with costs.
05. On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, my predecessor has framed the following Issues: ISSUES 01.

Whether petitioners prove that they are the LRs/dependents of deceased Sri.R.Karthik @
Rajendra Karthik?

02. Whether petitioners prove that deceased Sri.R.Karthik @ Rajendra Karthik died due to the injuries suffered in road traffic accident alleged to have been taken place on 09.12.2020 at about 11.00 p.m. at Ghat road, near Kukkaladoddi Village, Rly, Koduru Mandal, YSR Kadapa District,
Andra Pradesh, due to rash and negligent act of driving of the Car bearing registration No.AP39 BU0203 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
03. Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount & from whom?
04. What order or award?
Earlier, the mother of the deceased also shown as petitioner No.2 in the petition.

However,
subsequently she was reported to be dead and hence, her name was deleted from the cause title of the petition.

sentences.text: The petitioner No.1 who is the only son of the deceased is only legal heir and he was a minor, in order to prove their case, the paternal uncle and next friend of the petitioner No.1 is examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 11 documents as Ex.P.1 to 11 and closed their side evidence.
On behalf of the respondent No.2, its Assistant Manager got examined as RW.1 and through him 02 documents are marked as Ex.R.1 and 2 and closed its side evidence.
08. I have heard the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the petitioners and respondent No.2 and perused the records.

09. My findings on the above Issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.4 : As per final order

for the following:
 (SCCH3) 8 M.V.C.No.702/2021  REASONS 10. Issues No.1 and 2:

Since these two issues are interconnected to each other and in order to avoid repetition of facts and appreciation of evidence on record, these two issues are taken together for common consideration and discussion.
11. The petitioners in order to prove their case, the paternal uncle of the petitioner No.1 is examined as PW.1 and in his chiefexamination evidence he has reiterated the petition averments.

During the course of crossexamination by the respondent No.2 counsel he admits that the petitioner No.1 is his elder brother son and deceased Karthik is his elder brother and admits that as on the date of accident the deceased was driving the car, said car belongs to the friend of deceased and denied to the suggestion that said car was hired and admits that the deceased sustained injuries due to self accident and admits that the case and charge sheet were registered against the deceased and denied to the suggestion that there is no risk coverage for the driver under policy and only the risk of owner is covered and as the policy is PA coverage policy, he cannot claim compensation from the respondent and also denied to the suggestion that as (SCCH3) 9 M.V.C.No.702/2021 the accident occurred due to negligence of deceased only, hence they are not entitle for the compensation and as the accident occurred due to mechanical defect, the RC owner liable to pay compensation and not Insurance Company.
12.
Apart from the oral evidence, the PW.1 has got marked 11 documents as Ex.P.1 to 14.
Ex.P.1 is copy of FIR filed by the Rly Kodur Police, YSR District, Kadapa, against driver/deceased of offending Car for rash and negligent driving and death of deceased.
Ex.P.2 is copy of Complaint lodged against driver/deceased of offending Car.
Ex.P.3 is copy of Inquest Mahazar of deceased R.Karthik @ Rajendra Karthik.

Ex.P.4 is copy of Post mortem report of deceased R.Karthik @
Rajendra Karthik wherein it is stated that deceased died in road traffic accident and he was died due Kirthikeswar U vs T.V.Srinivasulu on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113504340/
4 to cardio respiratory failure due to hemorrhage shock due to intra cranial bleed, due to head injury.

Ex.P.5 is copy of Charge sheet which discloses that the Investigation Officer after thorough investigation has submitted abated Charge sheet against driver/deceased who is responsible for the accident who drove the car in rash and negligent manner and caused accident.

Ex.P.6 is copy of Driving licence of deceased which indicates that deceased (SCCH3) 10 M.V.C.No.702/2021 having a light motor vehicle nontransport driving licence which is valid till 29.05.2027, therefore, it appears that as on the date of accident the deceased had a valid driving licence to drive the car.
Ex.P.7 is copy of Aadhaar card of deceased.
Ex.P.8 is copy of Aadhaar card of petitioner No.1, which shows that the deceased is the father of the petitioner No.1.
Ex.P.9 is copy of Aadhaar card of PW.1.

Ex.P.10 is copy of family members certificate issued by the Tahsildar, Tirupati Rural, which shows that the petitioner No.1 is the only son and legal heir/dependent of the deceased Karthik and Ex.P.11 is copy of Death certificate of deceased Karthik which shows that he was died on 09.12.2020.

13. On going through the oral and documentary evidence adduced and produced by the PW.1, it clearly establishes that the petitioner No.1 who is the only survive legal heir and dependent of the deceased R.Karthik @ Rajendra Karthik and said petitioner No.1 is a minor and it is also proved that deceased R.Karthik @ Rajendra Karthik was died in road traffic accident that occurred on 09.12.2020, at about 11.00 p.m, at Ghatt Road, near Kukkaladoddi Village, Rly Kodur Mandal, YSR Kadapa District, Andra Pradesh, due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing No.AP39BU 0203, by the deceased himself.
Accordingly, these Issues No.1 & 2 are answered in the affirmative.
14. Issue No.3: This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the death of the deceased R.Karthik @ Rajendra Karthik, who died in the Motor Vehicle Accident.
15. In this case the death of deceased and alleged accident is not denied.

The only contention of the respondent No.2 Insurance Company is that the deceased driver is a tortfeasor and due to his rash and negligent driving of the car, he met with accident and died and there is no risk covered for the driver under the policy and only the risk of the owner is covered and as the policy is a PA coverage policy, the petitioner No.1 is not entitled for the compensation from the Insurance Company.
16.

To disprove the case of the petitioner No.1, on behalf of the respondent No.2, its Assistant Manager is examined as RW.1, wherein in his chiefexamination evidence he has reiterated the written statement averments by stating that risk under the personal accident is covered only for the owner cum driver but not other drivers of the insured car.
During the course of crossexamination by the  (SCCH3) 12 M.V.C.No.702/2021 petitioners counsel
he admits
that as on the date of accident the insurance policy of the offending vehicle is valid and is in force
and said policy is package policy and also admits that this payment of premium of Rs.820/ for 3 years coverage owner cum driver.

But denied to the suggestion that Kirthikeswar U vs T.V.Srinivasulu on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113504340/
5 deceased Karthik was a owner cum driver, Insurance Company is liable to pay compensation.

sentences.text: Further, he has produced copy of Policy, the said policy is a long term package policy - 3 years (private vehicle) policy and it is valid from 03.08.2019 to 09.12.2020.
It also appears that the alleged accident was occurred on 09122020, therefore, as on the date of accident the insurance policy of the offending car was valid and is in force.

It also appears that compulsory PA cover premium to owner cum driver 3 years, the premium amount of Rs.825/ has been paid and it indicates that said policy covered owner cum driver.
17.

The petitioner No.1 in order to substantiate his claim against the respondent No.2 Insurance Company, has relied upon the following citations:
01. (2009) 13 SCC 710 in between Ningamma and another V/s United India Insurance Company (SCCH3) 13 M.V.C.No.702/2021 Limited, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that, A. Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 - Ss.163A and 166 - Application of - Deceased driving a Motor Cycle which was borrowed from its real owner - Met with an accident by dashing against a bullock cart i.e., without involving any other vehicle - Claim under S.163A by legal representatives of deceased -

entities.text: Ningamma and another V/s United India Insurance Company (SCCH3) 13 M.V.C.No.702/2021 Limited
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Maintainability -

If not maintainable, then duty, if any, to consider claim under S.166, M.V Act, 1988 - Since deceased in present case had stepped into shoes of owner of vehicle, S.163A cannot apply wherein owner of vehicle himself is involved -
Hence, legal representatives of deceased could not have claimed compensation under S.163A -
However, even if S.163A was not applicable, High Court ought to have considered issues pertaining to claim under S.166 -
Since said issues were purely questions of fact, matter remitted to High Court.

02. AIR 2020 SC 527 (SC) in between Ramkhiladi and another V/s United India Insurance Company and another, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that, (SCCH3) 14 M.V.C.No.702/2021 Deceased is a permissible user or borrower of Motor vehicle which he was driving - Parties governed by contract of insurance - Liability of Insurance Company would be as per terms and conditions of contract of insurance only.

entities.text: Ramkhiladi and another V/s United India Insurance Company and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In para 5.8 it is held that, However, at the same time, even as per the contract of insurance, in case of personal accident the owner driver is entitled to a sum of Rs.1 lakh.
Therefore, the deceased, as observed herein above, who would be in the shoes of the owner shall be entitled to a sum of Rs. 1 lakh, even as per the contract of insurance.

03. 2018 AIR 2825 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Ashalata Bhowmik and others,
wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that, Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 - Section 166 - Claim application - Maintainability of - Death of owner insured when the vehicle he was driving met with accident and no other vehicle was involved -

Therefore, in the case on hand the contention of the Insurance Company is that owner driver means ownercumdriver is not acceptable. Therefore, the claimant is entitled to Rs.15,00,000/ as per PAC for owner.

(Paras 1, 2, 6 13, 15)
06. MFA No.8300/2011 (MV) c/w MFA No.6788/2011 (MV), MFA No.6789/2011 (MV) and MFA No.8301/2011 (MV) in between The United India Insurance Company Limited V/s Smt.N.Praveena and others, wherein the Hon'ble High Court in para 28 has held that, "As discussed at para 24 and 25, the petition under section 163A of M.V. Act is not maintainable against the respondents 1 and 2.

However, in the light of Ex.R.1, as per the terms of the contract of insurance between respondent No.1 and 2, respondent No.2 is liable to pay a sum of Rs.1,00,000/ covering the personal accident claim of the owner/driver, as the deceased stepped into the shoes of the owner in his capacity as the borrower of the offending vehicle".

Ltd., V/s Madhu.H.K and another, wherein it is held that, Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, section 163A  Claim application - Maintainability of  Borrower of vehicle  Injuries to  Son of insured  owner of motor cycle while driving the vehicle met with accident due to his own negligence and sustained injuries

sentences.text: Therefore, on going through the oral and documentary evidence of both the parties and as per Ex.R.2 insurance policy, it covers PA coverage of driver of Rs.15,00,000/.

19. In this case there is involvement of vehicle of the respondent No.1 and deceased R.Karthik was died in the accident and deceased was borrowed vehicle from the owner/respondent No.1 and deceased who stepped into shoes of the original owner of the said car and due to rash and negligent driving of the car by the deceased himself the accident occurred as evident from the Charge sheet.
Therefore, there exists a package policy covering the ownercumdriver, definitely the deceased is entitled for the said amount.
Further, on perusal of Ex.R.2 copy of policy produced by the respondent No.2 insurer there is a personal accident covered U/Sec III for registered ownercum driver for Rs.15,00,000/.

As per the above decision, the borrower i.e., the deceased in the present case stepped into shoes of the owner and covered under the policy as the deceased was driving the car by borrowing the same from the owner and he is covered under the (SCCH3) 19 M.V.C.No.702/2021 policy and consequently his legal representatives are entitled to the said amount.
20.

As discussed above, Ex.R.2 is a package policy covering the registered ownercumdriver i.e.,
the deceased in the present case who stepped into the shoes of the owner and was driving the car which involved in the accident and hence, as there is coverage of Rs.15,00,000/ under Ex.R.2, the petitioner No.1 is entitled for Rs.15,00,000/ and same is awarded to the petitioner No.1.
21.
As discussed above, it is the defence of the respondent No.2 that the deceased was drove the car belonging to the respondent No.1, hence, the deceased stepped into the shoes of the owner of the car.
Hence, respondent No.2 is not liable to pay compensation and the counsel for the respondent No.2 has also argued that petition U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act is not maintainable.

However, as stated supra, the counsel for the petitioner No.1 has relied upon decision in a case reported in AIR 2020 SC 527 (SC) in between Ramkhiladi and another V/s United India Insurance Company and another and as per the citations referred by the counsel for the petitioner No.1, the petitioner No.1 is entitled for compensation as per the (SCCH3) 20 M.V.C.No.702/2021 terms and conditions of the policy.

As per the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.2 which is in the name of the respondent No.1,
there is a insurance coverage for personal accident for owner and driver for Rs.15,00,000/.

When the deceased stepped into shoes of the owner of the insured car, as per the citations referred above,
the Insurance Company is liable to pay covered amount to the deceased.

The petitioner No.1 being the legal representative of the deceased R.Karthik @ Rajendra Karthik entitled for compensation of Rs.15,00,000/ with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
Accordingly, this Issue No.3 is answered partly in the affirmative.
22. Issue No.4:
In view of the above reasoning and discussions to the above Issues No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following: ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner No.1 under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner No.1 entitled for compensation of Rs.15,00,000/ (Rupees Fifteen lakhs only) with (SCCH3) 21 M.V.C.No.702/2021 interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.

opennyai_summary.facts:
On 09.12.2020 the deceased R.Karthik and his wife and son were going towards Tirupathi from Rly Kodur Town, in a Car bearing No.AP39BU0203 driven by deceased R.Karthik and said car belongs to family friends of deceased.
Due to impact the car was capsized and all the occupants of the car caught inside and sustained grievous injuries and J.Uma Maheswari and R.Karthik i.e.,
parents of petitioner No.1 succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
The accident was occurred due to carelessness, rash and negligent driving of the Car by its driver.
Prior to accident the deceased was hale and healthy and was aged 38 years and was businessman and earning Rs.50,000/ p.m and the petitioners are entirely depending upon the earnings of the deceased.

2 the tortfeasor and as such petition is liable to be dismissed.
Hence, claim petition is liable to be dismissed and (SCCH3)
5 M.V.C.No.702/2021 same is devoid of merits and admits the issuance of the policy in favour of respondent No.1 for the vehicle Car bearing No.AP39BU0203, but the same is subject to terms and conditions of the policy and as on the face of the prosecution papers reveals it is a self accident by the driver of the insured car and as such the question of coverage of liability to the petitioners by indemnifying the respondent No.1 does not arise at all under the personal accident coverage of Rs.15,00,000/ as claimed and also this is not a proper forum and hence, the liability is not admitted and claim against this respondent be dismissed as not maintainable and denied the entire case of the petitioners and denied alleged accident, age, occupation, income of deceased and expenses incurred by the petitioners and and also denied that deceased sustained fatal injuries in the alleged accident by driving insured car and the driver did not possess valid driving licence as on the date of accident and it is further contended that the place of accident is in the State of Andhra Pradesh, the Policy issuing office is at Delhi and owner is from Karnoon District of Andhra Pradesh State.
Hence, this Court has no jurisdiction to entertain the petition and the petition U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act is not maintainable, since Charge sheet is (SCCH3) 6 M.V.C.No.702/2021 against the deceased Karthik himself and due to his own negligence the alleged accident said to have occurred.
Hence, claim petition be dismissed as the tortfeasor is not entitle for compensation and the compensation claimed is exorbitant.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The only contention of the respondent No.2 Insurance Company is that the deceased driver is a tortfeasor and due to his rash and negligent driving of the car, he met with accident and died and there is no risk covered for the driver under the policy and only the risk of the owner is covered and as the policy is a PA coverage policy, the petitioner No.1 is not entitled for the compensation from the Insurance Company.
16.
If not maintainable, then duty, if any, to consider claim under S.166, M.V Act, 1988 - Since deceased in present case had stepped into shoes of owner of vehicle, S.163A cannot apply wherein owner of vehicle himself is involved -
Hence, legal representatives of deceased could not have claimed compensation under S.163A -
However, even if S.163A was not applicable, High Court ought to have considered issues pertaining to claim under S.166 -
03. 2018 AIR 2825 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Ashalata Bhowmik and others,
wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that, Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 - Section 166 - Claim application - Maintainability of - Death of owner insured when the vehicle he was driving met with accident and no other vehicle was involved -
ACJ 1319 of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in a case of Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Madhu.H.K and another, wherein it is held that, Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, section 163A  Claim application - Maintainability of  Borrower of vehicle  Injuries to  Son of insured  owner of motor cycle while driving the vehicle met with accident due to his own negligence and sustained injuries
As discussed above, Ex.R.2 is a package policy covering the registered ownercumdriver i.e.,
the deceased in the present case who stepped into the shoes of the owner and was driving the car which involved in the accident and hence, as there is coverage of Rs.15,00,000/ under Ex.R.2, the petitioner No.1 is entitled for Rs.15,00,000/ and same is awarded to the petitioner No.1.
21.
As discussed above, it is the defence of the respondent No.2 that the deceased was drove the car belonging to the respondent No.1, hence, the deceased stepped into the shoes of the owner of the car.
Hence, respondent No.2 is not liable to pay compensation and the counsel for the respondent No.2 has also argued that petition U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act is not maintainable.
When the deceased stepped into shoes of the owner of the insured car, as per the citations referred above,
the Insurance Company is liable to pay covered amount to the deceased.

opennyai_summary.decision:
In view of the above reasoning and discussions to the above Issues No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following: ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner No.1 under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner No.1 entitled for compensation of Rs.15,00,000/ (Rupees Fifteen lakhs only) with (SCCH3) 21 M.V.C.No.702/2021 interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this order.
On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, the entire share amount of the petitioner No.1 shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Schedule Bank till he attains age of majority with a liberty to draw accrued interest in the name of minor petitioner by his guardian on the said fixed deposit once in 3 months for the benefit of minor petitioner No.1.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.
